intent.title: Security monitoring of the whole 5G core (all catalog incidents)
intent.description: Detect and classify all thirteen incident types in the attack catalog across RAN, transport, control plane, user plane, service-based APIs and management, using telemetry from every network function, and hold every remediation for the operator together with its Indian reporting duties.

reference_points.4: ML underlay network (live simulation) ↔ ML pipeline: collector reads diagnostics; SINKs act
reference_points.1,2: simulated ML underlay networks ↔ ML pipeline in the sandbox subsystem
reference_points.3: ML sandbox subsystem ↔ ML pipeline subsystem: trained model handed over at deployment
reference_points.5: management subsystem (MLFO) ↔ ML pipeline subsystem: instantiation, model updates
reference_points.6: management subsystem (MLFO) ↔ ML sandbox subsystem: training, evaluation, selection
reference_points.7: MLFO ↔ other management functions: the incident-response engine (ir/engine.py) and its human gates

instantiation.chain: SRC → C → PP → M → P → D → SINK

selections.rule: highest macro_f1 among candidates with macro_f1 ≥ 0.85 and p95 inference ≤ 80.0 ms

card.description: Baseline: max per-feature z-score against normal operation with a trained threshold; nearest class centroid names the incident

notices.what: Report of the security incident with relevant details of the affected system and a description of the incident
notices.status: DRAFT — requires human review and sign-off; not sent
notices.phrase: within six hours of becoming aware of a security incident

notices.what: Details: (i) users affected, (ii) duration, (iii) geographical area, (iv) extent to which the network or service is affected, (v) remedial measures, (vi) other relevant information
notices.status: DRAFT — requires human review and sign-off; not sent
notices.phrase: within twenty-four hours of becoming aware

notices.what: Report of the cyber incident (if it is of a type listed in Annexure I of the Directions)
notices.instrument: CERT-In Directions under s.70B(6) IT Act, direction (ii)
notices.status: DRAFT — requires human review and sign-off; not sent
notices.phrase: within 6 hours of noticing such incidents

notices.what: Intimation of the security incident in the form and manner specified on the portal
notices.status: CONDITIONAL DRAFT — only if the affected element is notified as Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure
notices.source_check: verified in Critical Telecommunication Infrastructure Rules, 2024_0.pdf, p. 8
notices.phrase: no later than six hours of occurrence of such incident
notes: This deadline runs from OCCURRENCE, which may be earlier than detection; establish the occurrence time from the logs. The deadline shown is the latest possible.

notices.what: Description of the breach, likely consequences, mitigation, safety measures and a contact
notices.instrument: DPDP Act, 2023 s.8(6); DPDP Rules, 2025, rule 7(1)
notices.status: PREPAREDNESS DRAFT — duty not yet in force on the incident date
notices.phrase: intimate to each affected Data Principal
notes: DPDP breach duties come into force on 13 May 2027 (eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E), 13 Nov 2025); incident date 07 Oct 2026.

notices.what: Without delay: description of the breach — nature, extent, timing, location, likely impact
notices.status: PREPAREDNESS DRAFT — duty not yet in force on the incident date
notes: DPDP breach duties come into force on 13 May 2027 (eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E), 13 Nov 2025); incident date 07 Oct 2026.

notices.what: Updated and detailed information, facts and reasons, mitigation, findings about the person responsible, remedial measures, report of intimations to Data Principals
notices.status: PREPAREDNESS DRAFT — duty not yet in force on the incident date
notices.phrase: within seventy-two hours of becoming aware of the breach
notes: DPDP breach duties come into force on 13 May 2027 (eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E), 13 Nov 2025); incident date 07 Oct 2026.
